options.label: Park as STUCK, no rule reduction
options.consequence: No further spend. The formal half of the cryptid protocol (the rule reduction) stays undone, and the machine sits in the STUCK list rather than the cryptid list.

rationale: This is the case the cryptid protocol covers: formalize the rules, flag, and stop. Non-halting comes down to whether a coupled counter system avoids a sparse target set. The left counter u must miss O(1)-wide unsafe values at about one leading-O birth per doubling of Delta. The trajectory came within 2 sweeps of a configuration that is verified to halt (step 86,265). Later margins are only 7-13% of Delta, and the band edge sits on an unsafe point, so the obvious margin route is already closed. Heuristically the machine never halts, but no structural reason is known. Another search stage has poor odds, and stopping frees the budget for machines with validated mechanisms. The rule table itself is clean (1,096,578 sweeps exact to 1e10), so it is worth keeping as the write-up.

evidence.text: proof.md 3.3-3.4: Safe(w, 2g-1-d_1) can be decided on any single configuration, but it is not inductive. Configurations satisfying every proved clause still halt, e.g. Dep(1O100; 1; 11; 2,0) at step 940, and 85 of 323 random starts failing only this clause halted within 2e6 steps.
Step 86,265: Dep(O111000; 1; 111100; 9,4,2,0,0,0). The same configuration two sweeps later (word O111100) halts 18,861 steps on (unsafe_probe.c).
At marker-free ABS0 events, u/Delta fills [1.6066, 2.0006], and the 3/4 unsafe point is at 2.0. Margins at the five ABS0 events with a marker (to 1e10 sweeps): 2 sweeps, then 7-13% of Delta.
The rules are exact. GEN/ABS1/ABS0 match all 1,096,578 sweeps from step 2,000 to 1e10, random validation passes 8,540/8,540, and check_proof.py reports SUMMARY PASS 36/36.
